832  Part 4
Nutrition Therapy
Disorders of Fat Metabolism
Etiology and Clinical Manifestations
Fatty acids are transported into the mitochondria for oxidation 
via a complex system.81, 82 Th e fatty acids must be taken into 
the mitochondria using the carnitine transport system (see 
Figure 26.11). Carnitine palmitoyltransferase I (CPT 1) is an 
enzyme that allows a carnitine molecule to bind to a fatty acid 
molecule outside of the mitochondrion while releasing the co-
enzyme A segment. Th is acylcarnitine compound is then taken
into the mitochondrion via the carnitine acylcarnitine translo-
case enzyme. In the mitochondrion, another enzyme, carnitine 
palmitoyltransferase II (CPT 2), attaches the acylated fatty acid 
released from the carnitine with the coenzyme A segment. Th e 
carnitine is then released to allow for the transport of more 
fatty acids into the mitochondria.
